name: Eliezer
overview: Eliezer is a male figure identified as a descendant of Harim who had married a foreign wife. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or other personal notes. His mention in Ezra 10:31 situates him within the post-exilic community addressing intermarriage issues.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliezer means 'G-d is my help,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries significance in acknowledging divine assistance.
familyAndRelationships: Eliezer is explicitly noted as a descendant of Harim, establishing a genealogical link within the biblical record. Scripture does not record further family relationships for Eliezer beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Eliezer's significance lies in his representation of those within the returning exilic community who had married foreign wives, a matter addressed in Ezra 10:31. His inclusion highlights the challenges faced by Israel in maintaining covenantal purity and obedience to God's commands during the restoration period. As a descendant of Harim, his story contributes to understanding the broader narrative of faithfulness and reform among God's people.
